A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same STC paper. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original STC accuracy and latency evaluations in Tables 1–3, component ablations in Section 4.3, and additional experiments in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical evaluations, including the main benchmark comparisons and appendix ablations in Tables 6–10.

M1.justification: STC-Cacher and STC-Pruner retain the same procedures, components, and pseudocode. Figure 5 corrects labels without changing the method described in Section 3 and Algorithms 1–2.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same streaming and long-video tasks using OVO-Bench, StreamingBench, EgoSchema, MLVU-dev, and VideoMME. No additional dataset or test scenario appears.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding experiments: ToMe, VisionZip, and VidCom2 remain the compression baselines, with the same evaluated configurations of Dispider, LiveCC, StreamForest, and ReKV.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the 0.5 fps protocol, LLaVA-OV-7B backbone for ReKV, and existing cache/pruning settings. Its wording edits introduce no new or revised evaluation procedure.

E4.justification: The feature-reuse, dynamics-metric, and anchor ablations remain unchanged, as do Appendix B's cache-interval and hyperparameter studies. The qualitative examples in Figures 4 and 8 are also identical.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged, including the similarity-distribution summaries. Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All empirical tables and plots retain their values and findings. For example, Table 1 reports ReKV with combined STC at 52.0 overall, 78.3 seconds ViT encoding latency, and 263.7 seconds LLM prefilling latency in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–9 are unchanged, as are the mathematical operations in appendix Algorithms 1–2. No formal assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about joint ViT/LLM acceleration, plug-and-play compatibility, and accuracy–latency tradeoffs, including the stated 24.5% and 45.3% latency reductions.

C2.justification: Interpretations of temporal redundancy, feature reuse, dual-anchor scoring, cache-update frequency, and spatial–temporal balance remain unchanged. No substantive applicability boundary or limitation is added or removed.

D1.justification: The code link, documented model configurations, compression hyperparameters, and appendix implementation information are unchanged. Section 4.1 clarifies existing descriptions without disclosing new technical settings.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, related-work discussion, and positioning against existing streaming and token-compression methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 4.1 briefly refines the implementation paragraph, adding 'for efficient online inference' and explicitly mapping the two modules to their respective processing stages. The version/date stamp changes; document organization remains unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 5 swaps the reversed Compute/Reuse labels: Compute now points to the blue token, and Reuse to the yellow tokens, matching the legend. Small diagram alignment adjustments accompany this correction; other figures and all tables are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects Figure 5's misleading Compute/Reuse labels, making the diagram consistent with its legend and the described mechanism. Together with the small Section 4.1 clarification, this modestly improves explanatory accuracy. The methods, empirical evidence, and appendices otherwise remain unchanged.
